Digital tools are reshaping teaching methods and literacy practices. AI is increasingly used for complex data analysis in arts education.

results.title: Multimodal Analyses and Visual Models for Qualitatively ...
results.content: This paper presents three qualitative studies that use multimodal analyses and visual modeling to examine digital reading and writing across age groups, learning contexts, and literacy activities. Technologies are available that can provide multimodal data about students’ complex digital reading and writing processes, but often-employed research methods simplify the digital literacy problem space, specifically how individuals engage with digital texts and tools to read and communicate, rather than take advantage of the complexity (Shimizu et al., 2024; Sommer, 2021). To explore the multimodal analyses and visual models, we consider the digital reading process of one mid-level reader, Student H, across our three phases of analysis. However, the multimodal analysis and models showed Student H’s high quantity of highlights occurred across the whole digital text and corresponded with many instances of re-reading (Figure 3), which likely supported accurate returns to AOIs and overall strong comprehension outcomes (Figure 2).
